items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: We had Snooky Young, Clark Terry, myself and Emmett Berry.

ctx.x: Clark had been in the band.
Yes, he had been in the big band. Yeah. We had Snooky Young, Clark Terry, myself and Emmett Berry.
That was a good trumpet section.

items.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: when I didn‘t want to play a solo Sweets was in the band, he‘d play it.

ctx.x: One month. Young:…while Buck had his tonsils out. That‘s the first time. And the next time I went in the band I went in the band playing first trumpet because they knew I was a first trumpet player anyway. I came out of Lunceford‘s band playing first and so they, I told them, ―I don‘t want to play Buck Clayton‘s chair.‖ I said, ―He plays a lot of solos and different things.‖ ―That wasn‘t my thing,‖ I told them. They said, ―Come on Snooky, come on play it anyway.‖ So I played, and when I didn‘t want to play a solo…
One of the things about your sound is the way you use mutes.

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We had Al Grey, Snooky Young, and myself. Billy Mitchell, Eddie Jones, Marshall Royal.

ctx.x: But at least for that tour, you were able to….

It was a good band. It was a fantastic band and in fact, we had more Basie men in that band than was in the Frank Foster band. We had Al Grey, Snooky Young, and myself. Billy Mitchell, Eddie Jones, Marshall Royal.
